The must-sees

  • Adolphe Bridge

    Bridge · 1903

    Designed by Paul Séjourné and opened in 1903, it was the largest stone arch bridge in the world at the time. A suspended footbridge and cycle path was added under the deck in 2018.

    Look for: Look east along the valley to the older Passerelle viaduct, built around 1860 to link the old town with the new railway station.

  • Bock Casemates

    Fortress

    Count Siegfried built a castle on this rock in 963, the start of the city. The tunnels were dug from the 17th century and sheltered thousands of people during the air raids of both world wars.

    Look for: The Castle Bridge leading onto the Bock has two levels: a road on top and a covered passage beneath, so soldiers could cross unseen.

  • Chemin de la Corniche

    Viewpoint

    The path runs on top of 17th-century fortification walls. It is often called the finest balcony in Europe.

    Look for: Look down to the river: the long roofs of Neumünster Abbey, with the church of Saint-Jean beside it.

  • Grand Ducal Palace

    Palace · 1572

    It was built in 1572 as the town hall. Since 1890 it has been the official residence of the Grand Duke, who uses it for official work and state visits.

    Look for: The plainer building joined to the palace is the Chamber of Deputies, the country’s parliament.

  • Grund

    Neighbourhood

    Craftsmen, tanners and the city’s poorer residents once lived down here below the fortress. A public lift connects it to the upper town.

    Look for: From the river bank, look up at the Bock cliff and the openings of the casemates cut into the rock above you.

  • Gëlle Fra

    Landmark · 1923

    The monument honours Luxembourgers who volunteered in the First World War. The Nazis tore it down in 1940; its pieces were hidden and it was fully restored in 1985.

    Look for: At the foot of the obelisk, two bronze soldiers: one lies dead, the other keeps watch over him.

  • Neumünster Abbey

    Culture

    After the monks left it served for over a century as a prison, used by the Nazis during the occupation. It opened as a cultural meeting centre in 2004.

    Look for: Step into the church of Saint-Jean next door to find its Black Madonna.

  • Notre-Dame Cathedral

    Church

    It was built as a Jesuit church in the early 17th century and became a cathedral in 1870. Its crypt holds the grand ducal tombs and John the Blind, the count of Luxembourg who died at Crécy in 1346.

    Look for: Inside, find the robed statue of the Virgin, Comforter of the Afflicted, patron saint of the city and the country.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Luxembourg City and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Luxembourg City passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
